resolved.note: Rewrite checked line by line. Yeghiazar's rival claim matches Ormanian 4383-4388 ('At the same time ... supreme patriarch of Turkey, in opposition to Etchmiadzin'); 'the sultan's lands' for 'Turkey' is fair. Catholic use of the French ambassadors: Ormanian 4473-4475. Avedik jailed 1703 through the ambassador: Ormanian 4475-4478. 'Carried off to France' follows Ormanian ('secretly abducted ... taken to France') and Issaverdens 10009-10013 ('fell into the hands of the French ... took him to Marseilles'); 'where he died' rests on Chamich 21327-21333 (died a Capuchin at Marseilles), and Issaverdens (released, 'died in peace', no place) does not contradict it. Dropping 'meddling' was right. relationsSummary 61.4/7.8, longDescription 61.0/7.9.

'This defection' now refers to the two bishops going over to Rome, and the extended Ormanian quote (4469-4472) carries the referent. Abraham is named, with Ormanian 4526-4527 added. 'Ottoman lands' is in place. 'The other bishops of Sis ... They chose a rival' is closer to Issaverdens 10808-10813 ('bishops ... who had not taken part in his election ... elected one Michael') than my text; 'pontifical chair of Sis' at 10802-10804 confirms the see. The Serpos sentence keeps the source's force ('aver possono'). 64.2/7.5.
VII.24 teaser carries the text as given. It is in the test census. 65.6/8.0.
VII.24 continuesAs is null in the test census. The neighbor_changes row and the flag record the change and the Melkite precedent.

Grade Dominant Modern Reconstruction, not my Widely Accepted. Under the Drafting_Brief, Widely Accepted needs a primary source for the underlying facts. Chamich (1784-86) is some eighty years after 1703 and is cited as secondary elsewhere in this draft for events he did not live through (Gomidas, Alexander), so all five sources are secondary and DMR is the honest grade. My round-1 call was wrong on this point. The note's facts check out: 'without cause' (Chamich 21303-21305), thirty leading Armenians (21311-21314), beaten and stripped (21314-21319), island exile (Issaverdens 10006-10009, Tenedos). 'Catholic writers' is accurate (Chamich and Issaverdens are both Mekhitarists). major:false and minor_reason stand. 64.1/7.7.

The one-sentence outcome (24 words, 73.2/9.0) follows the one-sentence rule better than my two sentences did. 'The sultan's law' for 'sanzioni Sovrane' is fair, and it matches the relationsSummary. The Gomidas sentence now uses the Issaverdens source (10106-10111, John as subject), and Chamich 21449-21453 backs 'Catholic writers'. outcome_evidence = Serpos 384-387, the link's own quote. The flag that Serpos does not say the patriarchate asked for the decrees is right, and the outcome does not claim it. Note 66.5/7.6.

'Council of Chalcedon' is in Chamich 21375-21376 and Issaverdens 10050-10053. 'Respectful letter' is Issaverdens 10057-10060, and it is the more careful choice over Chamich's 'entire obedience' (21367-21369). 'Before he became head of the church' matches both texts ('previous to his elevation'). Dropping my 'c. 1715-25' was right: no vendored text dates Asdvadour. The corrected flag (the list runs to Asdvadour, 3375-3376) is accurate. Chamich is secondary for Alexander and primary for Simeon, consistent with A1-05. Documented still rests on the Jesuit memoir. 69.4/7.9.
'The pope approved a patriarch of their own for the Armenian Catholics', backed by Ormanian 4523-4536.

findings.issue: 'In 1860 a written Armenian statute set the bounds of each council's work' says the statute was in force in 1860. Ormanian 4795-4803 says only that it was 'finally worked into shape (1860)'. It needed Ottoman sanction, and only after 'three years of negotiations' did the Turkish Council give it effect (1863). A small slip in the date of force, but this is participant-facing fact.
